notes: An overlay on data/rosters.json, joined on team slug + MaxPreps athleteId. It never replaces a MaxPreps value: a field is filled only where MaxPreps has null, and where another source disagrees with MaxPreps the disagreement is recorded under conflicts and MaxPreps stays. The same rules apply to every league; a team with no public source beyond MaxPreps has empty lists.

Every filled value names its source URL, its kind (school-site, school-pdf, news, maxpreps-jv, maxpreps-career, maxpreps-team; maxpreps-career also covers MaxPreps' earlier-season roster pages, such as /field-hockey/25-26/roster/, which give a dated class year the same way, and maxpreps-jv is a JV roster page of either season) and a confidence: high = an official 2026-27 school roster or MaxPreps' own data for the same career; medium = a school-site profile field that is not season-dated, a school-paper statement, or a grade derived from a dated MaxPreps class year plus the years elapsed (derived: true); low = a profile field not tied to the season. For BVAL, PCAL and MCAL, a position that MaxPreps lists only for a PRIOR season (2025-26 roster, same career id) is not filled: positions change between seasons.

Names on a school roster that are not on MaxPreps are not added. JV rosters that school sites publish are out of scope, except that Los Gatos' MaxPreps list is the whole program and the school site says which rows are varsity and which JV. Where sources disagree on a grade MaxPreps leaves blank (a school page against MaxPreps' own earlier-season or career data, or a paper against either), the grade is left blank and every disagreeing source is recorded under the player's conflicts with kept: null; nothing is guessed.
si.com rosters were rejected: names only, and for several teams a different or prior-season list.

profiles[] links a player's own recruiting page (NCSA, SportsRecruits, Hudl), captured 2026-10-02 (SCVAL), 2026-10-03 (BVAL, PCAL, MCAL), 2026-10-04 (EAL) or 2026-10-06 (the Southern California teams). A page is linked only when it names the player and field hockey, and either names the player's school or shows the class year the roster shows plus a California hometown; a stated class year must agree with the roster's grade. NCSA pages answer a bot challenge, so SCVAL and PCAL NCSA profiles were matched on the search result (title, the school in the URL path, class year); for BVAL, MCAL and EAL the page itself was read where it answered. For the Southern California teams every linked page was read (NCSA through a headless browser), and a hometown with no state does not count as California. A Hudl profile counts when its team list includes this school's field hockey team, even if it lists another sport first. Social media, news and profiles for other sports are not linked. Recall is incomplete for every league: see docs/DATA-SOURCES.md.

A team's otherRosters says what other public sources showed for its CURRENT roster, which is what its page may claim when MaxPreps lists no players: none (looked, nothing current), partial (a source lists current players in a form that cannot be joined, with what it lists and a link) or, when absent, not checked.

EAL (2026-10-04): recruiting pages only (profiles[]), swept by the same rule. The school-athletics roster sweep (grade, height, number, position, coaches) has still not been done, so the six EAL entries have no coaches or sources and fill no MaxPreps field.

Southern California (2026-10-06): recruiting pages only (profiles[]), swept by the same rule for the 53 teams (the Sunset, City, North and Metro teams and the five Southern Section independents): 267 pages for 202 players. Each page was re-read by two independent verifiers, one checking it against the rule and one trying to refute it, and kept only when both kept it. The school-athletics roster sweep (grade, height, number, position, coaches) has not been done for them, so their entries have no coaches or sources and fill no MaxPreps field.

2026-10-12: profiles in any sport. Until then only field hockey profiles were linked; since 2026-10-12 a profile in another sport is linked too and names its sport (a field hockey profile names none), at most one per platform in each sport. A SportsRecruits profile-address probe ran in every sport (the first_last slug and its numbered variants) for all 1,673 varsity rows (1,355 at first, the other 318 later the same day, after the environment's two-hour limit stopped the first run). A page was kept when its title names the player, its class year agrees with the roster (2027-2030 for a row with no grade), and it names the school's own team or gives a hometown in the school's own area (San Diego County, Greater Los Angeles, the Bay Area and Central Coast, or the Sacramento Valley and north state). A player whose matching pages disagree on the hometown kept only the pages in the school's own city, and a known namesake (the other class-of-2027 Phoebe Miller, in San Francisco) was left out. Soccer, track and volleyball pages were kept only where the club named is a girls' club (one volleyball page, from Santa Maria for a La Verne school, was left out). 119 pages for 117 players were kept, each re-read (one, Grace Martinez's softball page, was unlinked later that day when Thousand Oaks' roster gave her another class; 118 for 116 remain): 91 lacrosse, 16 softball, 6 field hockey, 5 soccer, 1 track and field. NCSA, Hudl and FieldLevel were not probed in other sports: their addresses cannot be guessed.

2026-10-12: grades from MaxPreps' own pages for the 413 varsity rows MaxPreps' 2026-27 roster leaves ungraded and nothing had filled. Each row's MaxPreps career page (graduatingClass, and the grade of every team it lists for a dated season, in any sport) and the team's 2025-26 and 2024-25 MaxPreps field hockey rosters (matched on careerId, or on the name where the page has one row of it) were read; the grade is that season's plus the seasons since. 137 rows got a grade where every such page agreed (kind maxpreps-career, derived, medium; each note ends 'Added 2026-10-12.'). Two rows whose pages disagree are left blank with both recorded under conflicts (Izabel Gaytan, Ellie Kay); three whose 2025-26 or 2024-25 roster would make them 13th-graders are left blank (Emma Steingraber, Brooke Flesuras, Sarah Anton); seven rows that already carried grade conflicts were left as they were; and Michelle MacOubray's grade stays blank because her career page and her SportsRecruits page disagree.

2026-10-12, second pass: the rows still ungraded after the MaxPreps pass (266) were looked up on their schools' own athletics sites (2026-27 rosters first, then 2025-26 ones carried forward), in school papers and in local news, by the rule above. 113 got a grade: 95 from school sites (Glendora's, Granite Hills' and Southwest's player pages, Helix's, Bonita's, Cathedral Catholic's and Great Oak's rosters, Thousand Oaks' 2025-26 roster, Clairemont's and Saratoga's sites, Huntington Beach's program site) and 18 from school papers and news (the Talon, the Epitaph, the Pitch, the Redwood Bark, the San Diego Union-Tribune, Times of San Diego). Medium, not high, where the page is not the school's own season roster: Southwest's Home Campus site, which the school homepage does not link; Cathedral Catholic's site, which keeps one grade per player rather than per season; three Great Oak players its site lists on JV while MaxPreps has them on varsity; and every paper. A story that is not about field hockey was used only for an exact name at the same school, and says so. Left blank and recorded under conflicts: Paula Mata (Glendora; her profile's grade disagrees with its own team history), Teagan Dickison Elias (Salinas; two profiles of her disagree), and Emma Steingraber and Brooke Flesuras (Granite Hills' site says grade 12, MaxPreps' 2025-26 roster had them as seniors). Not used: a story read only from a search engine's copy (Elsie Edelson), and grades for three duplicate MaxPreps rows whose twin MaxPreps already grades. Grace Martinez's SportsRecruits softball page (class of 2029) was unlinked when Thousand Oaks' roster made her grade 11. 164 varsity rows still have no grade from any source.

2026-10-13: claimed MaxPreps pages. Every row's MaxPreps career page (1,702, the careerUrl in data/rosters.json) was read for its isClaimed flag, which marks a page the player or a parent has claimed on MaxPreps (the page then shows MaxPreps' Claimed badge). The 260 claimed pages, on 73 teams, are linked as profiles with platform maxpreps: the row's own careerUrl, no sport (one page covers every sport), classOf the page's graduatingClass where it gives one (221). They need no name match, being the page the row comes from; lib/rosters.ts refuses one whose URL is not its row's careerUrl. One page (Marin Catholic's Alexandra Schmidt) answered 403 and is not linked. An unclaimed career page is not linked: MaxPreps keeps one for every rostered player.

2026-11-03: another SportsRecruits profile-address probe in every sport over all 1,673 varsity rows (23,270 addresses: the first_last slug, hyphen and multi-word variants, each with no suffix and 1 to 12; 670 live, 649 pages read after dropping men's lacrosse). A page was kept by the 2026-10-12 rule (title names the player, class year agrees, and it names the school's own team or gives a hometown in the school's own area), at most one per platform in each sport, and each kept page was re-read by an independent refuter, who kept all of them. 30 pages for 30 players were linked (14 NorCal, 16 SoCal): 26 lacrosse, 3 field hockey and 1 soccer. Most were live before 2026-10-12 and that day's probe did not link them (among them the own profiles of six committed players: Storey Lewis' lacrosse page and those of Gigi Colant, Catherine Cecchini, Kaye Zilinskas, Violet Potts and Emerson Davis); Charlotte Painter's field hockey page (Fremont) was created 2026-10-25. Two lacrosse pages linked on 2026-10-12 had moved (abigail_wisbach and reagan_roach now answer Page Not Found) and were re-linked at their new addresses. Bare pages (a class year and no school or place: Anaai Trujillo, Elliot Gould, a second Emerson Davis page) and namesakes in other states were not linked. Every SportsRecruits page already linked was re-read: all 228 answer, and none shows a commitment the file lacks. NCSA, Hudl and FieldLevel were not probed, and the claimed-MaxPreps read of 2026-10-13 was not repeated: MaxPreps answered the career-page re-read with HTTP 403 after a few dozen pages, so it was stopped.

Coaches had entered grades this file supplied for 48 players (Saratoga 21, Berkeley 12, Mission Bay 9, University City 6), every one equal to the recorded value, so those notes were dropped: MaxPreps now gives the grade. 2026-11-13: Hudl's public team rosters and NCSA's field hockey school pages, for all 102 schools. Hudl was read through its public GraphQL endpoint (the one its public fan pages use; the doc's EAL route), every field hockey team of the 88 schools with rows, the current season's roster or, where a team has none, its latest (Christopher's team is labelled 2023 and Convent & Stuart Hall's 2022 even on profiles created in 2026). 78 public profiles of varsity-file rows not linked before were kept, each listing a field hockey team at the row's school, its overview naming the school, and its class year agreeing with the roster (Christopher's Johanna Canseco's page gives none; it names the school): Christopher 15, University 15, Saint Francis 13, Gilroy 9, Valley Christian 7, Berkeley 5 (all on Berkeley's JV team on Hudl; Sage Murphy was on the JV list when the sweep ran and joined the varsity roster the same day), Convent 5, Mitty 4, St. Ignatius 3, Marin Catholic 1 (Lexie Schmidt, class of 2027) and Pleasant Valley 1. Given-name pages (Madison McDougall, Addison Paradiso, Alexandra Pires, Lexie Osaki) are linked on the school and class year. NCSA's school pages (read through WebFetch, 99 pages for the 88 schools, with the right slugs where a name redirects to a namesake school elsewhere: Valley Christian's are -10 and -7, Southwest's is southwest-senior-high-school) added four field hockey pages, each naming the school with a class year that agrees: Samantha Brunsell (St. Ignatius), Eleanor Navarrette (Mitty), Junali Dutta (Lynbrook) and Myla McCandless (Bishop's). An independent refuter re-opened every page and kept every one. Not linked: 96 Hudl roster entries of rostered players whose profiles are private (Valley Christian 22, La Costa Canyon 16, Pleasant Valley 9 and others); Hudl pages whose class year disagrees with the roster (among them four La Jolla Country Day pages a year earlier than the rows, which may mean the grades are off); second Hudl profiles for rows that already link one; NCSA listings with no profile address that answers (Dylan Powell, Maggie Magnano, Brooklyn Barnard, Charlotte Painter, Kasia Umholtz); and 16 FieldLevel pages from an address probe of the 1,688 varsity rows then on file, which give no class year or school. JV players' pages from the same sweep are in data/jv-profiles.json.

2026-11-13, a search of four schools (Sobrato, Cupertino, Lynbrook and Homestead; 116 players: 72 varsity rows, 44 JV), the 20 Sobrato rows new to the roster that day: a SportsRecruits address probe in every sport (4,550 addresses, name variants and suffixes 1 to 12, every live page read, the bare ones also rendered twice under the 2026-11-13 rule), every Hudl team of the four schools in every sport for 2022 to 2026 and a Hudl name search for every player, NCSA's field hockey, lacrosse, soccer, softball, volleyball and basketball school pages and a guessed address for every player, and FieldLevel in eight sports. Six pages for five players were kept, each naming the school with a class year that agrees, and an independent refuter kept all six: Sobrato's Cameron Isle (Hudl and NCSA basketball), Lynbrook's Grace Cho (Hudl soccer), Cupertino's Allenah Watkins (NCSA field hockey, not on NCSA's school list), and Homestead's Olivia Leyton Bravo (NCSA field hockey) and Aalya Jain (NCSA softball). Not linked: an NCSA address under Sobrato goalkeeper Kinzie Rasley's name that serves a page headed 'Regan Stuart '28' (Sobrato field hockey goalkeeper, class of 2028) with her name nowhere on it; bare SportsRecruits pages (a class year, no school or place, even rendered); a private Hudl profile (Rebecca Frelich); namesakes. Grades the same day: Homestead's Sarah Anton (12), Sahana Gopinath (11), Renee Lam (10) and Elle Correia (10) from Stick Together's 2025 all-league lists (derived), and Olivia Leyton Bravo (10) and Rhea Ananthateerta (10) from The Epitaph's Nov 2, 2026 game review; Lynbrook's Trishna Sinha and Sahana Rajamani keep the school site's grade 11 (owner decision), with Stick Together's 2025 list, which would make Sinha 12 and Rajamani 10, recorded as conflicts.

2026-11-26, the players no sweep had reached: the 75 varsity rows MaxPreps added on 2026-11-13 at 22 schools (not Sobrato’s 20, searched that day, nor the six JV-list players who joined their varsity rosters), and the 40 players of Marina’s and Newport Harbor’s own 2026 varsity lists (otherRosters `listed`). Sources: a SportsRecruits address probe in every sport (about 2,650 addresses, suffixes to 12 or 15, nicknames), every Hudl team of the 24 schools in every sport and season 2021 to 2026 through its public GraphQL endpoint plus a Hudl name search for every player, NCSA’s school pages and a name address for every player, FieldLevel, MAX Field Hockey, and each MaxPreps row’s career page for its claimed flag (MaxPreps answered 403 to about half the requests; every page loaded on spaced retries). Each kept page was read twice by the pass that found it and re-opened by an independent refuter, which kept all 34. Linked: 19 pages for 14 MaxPreps rows (8 claimed MaxPreps pages: Hollister’s Gabriella Sanchez, Corning’s Harley Slye, Shelby Peterson, Makayla Lodin, Aliza Thuemler and Anaya Sherrod, Lassen’s Austan Mueller and Mt. Harper Morris’s NCSA page (2029) and Teagan Joob’s (2028) each disagree by a year with a private Hudl roster entry; both stay linked with the conflict in their note. 20 of the 75 rows also sit on MaxPreps’ JV rosters, as 147 varsity rows do; pages go on the varsity row as before.
